questions.prompt: Are you usually on time for appointments?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I am on time. For work. Always.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I try to be on time. But sometimes I am late. Because the bus is late. And I don't like to be late, but it happens.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I usually try to be on time for appointments. I think it's important to be respectful of other people's time. However, sometimes things happen and I'm a little late, for example if the traffic is bad. But I always try my best to be punctual.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, I'm usually pretty punctual. I really hate keeping people waiting, so I tend to set off a little early, just in case. That said, the traffic here can be a nightmare, so every now and then I turn up a few minutes late. In that case, I always give them a heads-up.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Men vaqtida boraman. Ishga. Har doim.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Ha, men vaqtida bo'lishga harakat qilaman.
Lekin ba'zida men kechikaman.
Chunki avtobus kechikadi.
Va men kechikishni yoqtirmayman, lekin shunday bo'lib qoladi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, men odatda uchrashuvlarga o'z vaqtida borishga harakat qilaman. O'ylashimcha, boshqa odamlarning vaqtini hurmat qilish muhim.
Biroq, ba'zida shunday holatlar bo'ladiki, men biroz kechikaman, masalan, agar tirbandlik yomon bo'lsa. Lekin men har doim o'z vaqtida bo'lishga bor kuchim bilan harakat qilaman.
questions.uzSampleB2: Odatda, men uchrashuvlarga o'z vaqtida yetib borishga harakat qilaman. Men vaqtida bo'lishni hurmat va yaxshi tashkilotchilik belgisi deb bilaman. Albatta, kutilmagan holatlar rejamni buzishi mumkin, masalan, jamoat transportida kutilmagan kechikishlar yoki juda tirbandlik. Bunday vaziyatlarda men har doim kechikish haqida imkon qadar tezroq xabar berishga harakat qilaman. Umuman olganda, vaqtida bo'lish men uchun muhim.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Are you usually on time for appointments?
idioms: Better three hours too soon than a minute too late - "Bir daqiqa kech qolganidan uch soat oldin borgan yaxshi"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I generally try to be punctual for..." - "Ha, men odatda ... uchun vaqtida bo'lishga harakat qilaman"
"I usually set reminders..." - "Men odatda eslatmalar o'rnataman..."
"However, I must admit that..." - "Biroq, tan olishim kerakki..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I generally try to be punctual for all my appointments. I believe that being on time shows respect for other people's schedules.
I usually set reminders on my phone about 30 minutes before any meeting or appointment. This gives me enough time to prepare and make my way to the destination without rushing.
However, I must admit that heavy traffic in Tashkent can sometimes make it difficult to arrive right on the dot. As they say, "Better three hours too soon than a minute too late".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, men odatda barcha uchrashuvlarimga o'z vaqtida borishga harakat qilaman. Menimcha, vaqtida bo'lish boshqa odamlarning jadvaliga hurmat ko'rsatadi.

Men odatda har qanday uchrashuv yoki appointmentdan taxminan 30 daqiqa oldin telefonimda eslatmalar o'rnataman. Bu menga tayyorgarlik ko'rish va shoshilmasdan manzilga yetib borish uchun yetarli vaqt beradi.

Biroq, tan olishim kerakki, Toshkentdagi tirbandlik ba'zan aynan vaqtida yetib borishni qiyinlashtirishi mumkin. Aytishlaricha, "Bir daqiqa kechikkaningdan ko'ra, uch soat oldin kelgan yaxshiroq".

questions.prompt: How many languages can you speak?
questions.sampleA2: I speak English. And I learn Spanish in school, but it's not very good.
questions.sampleB1: I can speak two languages. I speak English, of course, and I also speak a little bit of French. I learned French in high school. I think it's a beautiful language, however, I'm not very fluent.
questions.sampleB2: I can get by in three languages, to be honest. Uzbek is my mother tongue, and I use Russian pretty much every day, so I'd say I'm fairly fluent in both. English is the one I'm still working on, but I've picked up quite a lot over the years and I can hold my own in most conversations.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men bitta tilda gaplasha olaman. Ingliz tili.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men ingliz tilida gaplasha olaman. Va men maktabda ispan tilini o'rganaman, lekin u juda yaxshi emas.
questions.uzSampleB1: Men ikki tilda gaplasha olaman. Men ingliz tilida gaplashaman, albatta, va men biroz fransuz tilida ham gaplashaman. Men fransuz tilini o'rta maktabda o'rganganman. Menimcha, bu juda go'zal til, lekin, men unchalik ravon gapira olmayman.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men ikki tilda ravon gaplasha olaman: ingliz va ispan. Ispan tili mening ona tilim, ingliz tilida esa bolaligimdan beri gaplashaman. Shuningdek, nemis tilidan ham biroz xabarim bor, uni bir necha yil o'rganganman, lekin men uni haqiqatan ham gaplasha olaman deb ayta olmayman. Garchi men oddiy suhbatlarni tushuna olsam ham, murakkab gaplarni tuzish men uchun hali ham qiyinchilik tug'diradi.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - How many languages can you speak?
idioms: A different language is a different vision of life - "Boshqa til - hayotning boshqa ko'rinishi"
sentenceStarters: "I can speak three languages with..." - "Men uchta tilni ... darajada bilaman"
"My mother tongue is..." - "Mening ona tilim..."
"I'm currently working on improving..." - "Men hozirda ... ni yaxshilash ustida ishlayman"

questions.sampleAnswer:
I can speak three languages with varying degrees of fluency. My mother tongue is Uzbek, which I use daily with my family and friends.
I also speak Russian quite well, as it's widely used in my country for business and education. Additionally, I've been learning English for several years now, and I'd say my level is upper-intermediate.
I'm currently working on improving my English because I believe that being multilingual opens many doors in terms of career opportunities and cultural understanding. As they say, "A different language is a different vision of life".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Men uchta tilda turli darajadagi ravonlik bilan gaplasha olaman. Mening ona tilim o'zbek tili, undan oilam va do'stlarim bilan har kuni foydalanaman.

Men rus tilida ham yaxshi gaplasha olaman, chunki u mening mamlakatimda biznes va ta'lim uchun keng qo'llaniladi. Bundan tashqari, men bir necha yildan beri ingliz tilini o'rganib kelyapman va menimcha, mening darajam yuqori o'rta daraja.

Men hozirda ingliz tilimni yaxshilash ustida ishlayapman, chunki ko'p tillarni bilish martaba imkoniyatlari va madaniy tushunish nuqtai nazaridan ko'plab eshiklarni ochadi deb hisoblayman. Aytishlaricha, "Har xil til - hayotga har xil qarash".

questions.prompt: What is your favorite color and why?
questions.sampleA2: My favorite color is red. I like red because it is bright. And it's the color of my car. I also like red flowers.
questions.sampleB1: My favorite color is green. I think it's a really nice color because it reminds me of nature, like trees and grass. I also like that it's a calming color. For example, when I'm stressed, I like to go for a walk in the park where there is lots of green.
questions.sampleB2: I suppose my favourite colour has to be green. There's something about it that I find really calming — it instantly brings to mind forests, fields and the outdoors, which I absolutely love. On top of that, it's easy on the eye and it goes with almost anything, so I tend to gravitate towards it when I'm buying clothes.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menga ko'k rang yoqadi. Ko'k rang yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Mening sevimli rangim qizil. Qizil rang menga yoqadi, chunki u yorqin. Va bu mening mashinamning rangi. Qizil gullar ham menga yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Mening eng sevimli rangim yashil. Menimcha, bu juda yoqimli rang, chunki u menga tabiatni, masalan, daraxtlar va o'tlarni eslatadi. Menga uning tinchlantiruvchi rang ekanligi ham yoqadi.
Misol uchun, men stressda bo'lganimda, yashillik ko'p bo'lgan parkda sayr qilishni yaxshi ko'raman.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Menimcha, mening eng sevimli rangim, ehtimol, binafsha rang. Men uni juda qiziqarli deb bilaman. U ko'k yoki yashil kabi keng tarqalgan emas, lekin unda ma'lum bir chuqurlik bor.

O'ylaymanki, menga yoqishining bir sababi uning ijodkorlik va xayolot bilan bog'liqligi. U sizni qutidan tashqarida fikrlashga undaydigan rangga o'xshaydi. Bundan tashqari, soyasiga qarab, u ham yorqin, ham tinchlantiruvchi bo'lishi mumkin, bu menga juda yoqadi.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - What is your favorite color and why?
idioms: Colours are the smiles of nature - "Ranglar tabiatning tabassumi"
sentenceStarters: "My favourite colour is definitely..." - "Mening sevimli rangim, albatta..."
"I think the main reason is that..." - "Menimcha, asosiy sabab shuki..."
"Moreover, it is a very versatile colour..." - "Bundan tashqari, bu juda ko'p qirrali rang..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
My favourite colour is definitely blue. I've been drawn to this colour for as long as I can remember.
I think the main reason is that blue naturally evokes a sense of calm and tranquillity. Whenever I look at a clear blue sky or the sea, I feel incredibly relaxed and at peace.
Moreover, blue is a very versatile colour – it works well in clothing, interior design, and even in branding. Many people associate it with trust and reliability, which is why so many companies use it in their logos. As they say, "Colours are the smiles of nature".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Mening eng sevimli rangim, albatta, ko'k. Men o'zimni eslay olganimdan beri bu rangga qiziqib kelaman.

O'ylashimcha, asosiy sababi shundaki, ko'k rang tabiiy ravishda xotirjamlik va osoyishtalik hissini uyg'otadi. Har safar tiniq moviy osmonga yoki dengizga qarasam, o'zimni juda xotirjam va tinch his qilaman.

Bundan tashqari, ko'k rang juda ko'p qirrali rang – u kiyimda, interyer dizaynida va hatto brendingda ham yaxshi ishlaydi. Ko'pchilik uni ishonch va ishonchlilik bilan bog'laydi, shuning uchun ham ko'plab kompaniyalar o'z logotiplarida undan foydalanadi. Aytishlaricha, "Ranglar tabiatning tabassumidir".

questions.prompt: What do you see in these pictures?
questions.sampleA1: I see people. One person is teaching. Another person uses computer.
questions.sampleA2: I see two pictures. In one picture, a man is teaching a woman. And in the other picture, a woman is using a computer. Maybe she is learning something. It is different.
questions.sampleB1: Okay, in the first picture, there's a person showing another person how to do something, maybe a craft or a trade. I think it's a traditional way of learning. However, in the second picture, the person is learning by themselves using a computer. It seems like they are taking an online course. It's a more modern approach, in my opinion.
questions.sampleB2: The first picture shows an older woman, likely a grandmother, sharing a moment with a young girl in a bright, modern kitchen. They are baking together, with the girl pouring milk into a bowl while the woman stirs. It’s a clear example of intergenerational learning, where practical skills are passed down directly. In contrast, the second image features a man in a workshop, focused on a laptop displaying a video tutorial. A bicycle is on a repair stand next to him, and tools are scattered around. This suggests he’s taking on a repair task independently. Both scenes illustrate learning, but one is a warm, shared activity, while the other involves solitary, tech-assisted skill development.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men odamlarni ko'ryapman. Bir odam o'rgatyapti. Boshqa odam kompyuterdan foydalanyapti.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men ikki rasm ko'ryapman. Bir rasmda, bir erkak ayolga o'rgatyapti. Va boshqa rasmda, bir ayol kompyuterdan foydalanyapti. Balki u nimadir o'rganyapti. Bu boshqacha.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Xo'sh, birinchi rasmda bir odam boshqa odamga nimadir qilishni o'rgatayapti, ehtimol hunar yoki kasb. Menimcha, bu o'rganishning an'anaviy usuli.
Ammo, ikkinchi rasmda odam kompyuterdan foydalanib, o'zi o'rganyapti. Ko'rinishidan, ular onlayn kurs o'tayapti. Mening fikrimcha, bu zamonaviyroq yondashuv.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Rasmlar an'anaviy va zamonaviy o'qitish usullarini solishtiradiganga o'xshaydi. Birinchi rasmda kimdir bevosita ta'lim olayotgani tasvirlangan, ehtimol kasbiy mahorat bo'yicha. Bu ko'proq amaliy, shogirdlik uslubidagi yondashuvni anglatadi. Ikkinchi rasm,
lekin, kompyuter orqali mustaqil ravishda o'rganayotgan odamni ko'rsatadi. Bu o'z-o'zini boshqaradigan, ehtimol onlayn ta'lim muhitini taklif qiladi, bu esa ko'proq moslashuvchanlik va ma'lumotga kirish imkonini beradi. Har bir yondashuvning afzalliklari va kamchiliklarini ko'rib chiqish qiziq.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - What do you see in these pictures?
sentenceStarters: "These pictures illustrate different approaches to..." - "Bu rasmlar ... ga turli yondashuvlarni ko'rsatadi"
"In the first picture, I can see..." - "Birinchi rasmda men ... ko'ryapman"
"The second picture shows..." - "Ikkinchi rasm ... ko'rsatadi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
These two pictures illustrate different approaches to acquiring new skills.
In the first picture, I can see a person learning a practical skill directly from an experienced individual, probably a mentor or instructor. They appear to be working together in a hands-on setting, which suggests a traditional apprenticeship style of learning where knowledge is passed on through direct interaction.
The second picture shows someone learning independently, likely using online resources or tutorials on a computer. This represents a more modern, self-directed approach to education where people can learn at their own pace from the comfort of their home.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu ikki rasm yangi ko'nikmalarni egallashning turli yondashuvlarini ko'rsatib beradi.

Birinchi rasmda men tajribali shaxsdan, ehtimol ustoz yoki o'qituvchidan bevosita amaliy ko'nikmani o'rganayotgan odamni ko'rishim mumkin. Ular amaliy sharoitda birga ishlayotganga o'xshaydi, bu bilim bevosita muloqot orqali o'tkaziladigan an'anaviy shogirdlik uslubini ko'rsatadi.

Ikkinchi rasmda esa kimdir mustaqil ravishda, ehtimol kompyuterda onlayn resurslar yoki darsliklardan foydalanib o'rganayotganini ko'rsatadi. Bu ta'limga nisbatan yanada zamonaviy, o'z-o'zini boshqaradigan yondashuvni ifodalaydi, bunda odamlar o'z uylarida qulay sharoitda o'z sur'atlarida o'rganishlari mumkin.

questions.prompt: What are the benefits of learning practical skills directly from an experienced person?
questions.sampleA1: I learn from my father. He knows cars. He helps me fix my bike. It is good.
questions.sampleA2: I think it's good to learn from someone old. They know more things and they can show you. My grandma teaches me to cook. It's better than reading a book because she can help me.
questions.sampleB1: I think it's really useful to learn from someone who has experience. For example, if you want to learn how to play guitar, a good teacher can show you the right techniques. Also, they can give you advice based on their own mistakes. In my opinion, it's much faster than learning by yourself from the internet.
questions.sampleB2: The thing is, when you learn straight from someone experienced, you get instant feedback — they can spot your mistakes and put you right on the spot. You also pick up little tricks of the trade that you'd never find in a textbook. On top of that, they keep you motivated, so you're far less likely to give up when things get tricky.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men otamdan o'rganaman. U mashinalarni biladi. U menga velosipedimni tuzatishga yordam beradi. Bu yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menimcha, keksa odamdan o'rganish yaxshi. Ular ko'proq narsalarni bilishadi va sizga ko'rsatib bera olishadi. Mening buvim menga ovqat pishirishni o'rgatadi. Bu kitob o'qigandan yaxshiroq, chunki u menga yordam bera oladi.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, tajribaga ega bo'lgan odamdan o'rganish juda foydali.
Masalan, agar siz gitara chalishni o'rganmoqchi bo'lsangiz, yaxshi o'qituvchi sizga to'g'ri texnikalarni ko'rsatishi mumkin. Shuningdek, ular o'z xatolariga asoslanib, sizga maslahat berishlari mumkin.
Mening fikrimcha, bu internetdan o'zingiz o'rganishdan ancha tezroq.
questions.uzSampleB2: Tajribali odamlardan amaliy ko'nikmalarni o'rganishning afzalliklari, albatta, bor. Birinchidan, ular shaxsiy yo'l-yo'riq berishlari va o'z ta'limotlarini sizning aniq ehtiyojlaringiz va o'rganish uslubingizga moslashtirishlari mumkin. Bu kitob qila olmaydigan narsa. Ikkinchidan, tajribali odam qo'llanmalarda yoki onlayn manbalarda har doim ham aniq ko'rsatilmagan nozik bilim va tushunchalarni bera oladi. Bundan tashqari, savollar berish va darhol javob olish imkoniyati bebaho bo'lib, o'rganish jarayonini sezilarli darajada tezlashtiradi.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - What are the benefits of learning practical skills directly from an experienced person?
idioms: Experience is the best teacher - "Tajriba eng yaxshi o'qituvchi"
sentenceStarters: "There are numerous benefits to..." - "... ning ko'plab foydalari bor"
"Firstly, an experienced mentor can provide..." - "Birinchidan, tajribali ustoz ... ta'minlay oladi"
"Furthermore, learning from a person builds..." - "Bundan tashqari, insondan o'rganish ... ni shakllantiradi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
There are numerous benefits to learning practical skills directly from someone with experience, much like the scene in the first picture.
Firstly, an experienced mentor can provide immediate feedback and correct mistakes on the spot, which significantly speeds up the learning process. When you're learning something hands-on, like cooking or carpentry, having someone guide you in real time is invaluable.
Secondly, experienced people can share practical tips and tricks that you simply won't find in textbooks or online tutorials. These are often lessons learned through years of trial and error.
Furthermore, learning from a person builds a personal connection and often leads to valuable networking opportunities. As they say, "Experience is the best teacher", and learning from those who have it is the next best thing.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Tajribali odamdan bevosita amaliy ko'nikmalarni o'rganishning ko'plab foydalari bor, xuddi birinchi rasmdagi kabi.

Birinchidan, tajribali ustoz darhol fikr-mulohaza bildira oladi va xatolarni joyida tuzatishi mumkin, bu esa o'rganish jarayonini sezilarli darajada tezlashtiradi. Agar siz qo'lda biror narsa o'rganayotgan bo'lsangiz, masalan, ovqat pishirish yoki duradgorlik, kimdir sizga real vaqtda yo'l-yo'riq ko'rsatishi juda qimmatli.

Ikkinchidan, tajribali odamlar siz darsliklarda yoki onlayn darslarda topa olmaydigan amaliy maslahatlar va usullarni baham ko'rishlari mumkin. Bular ko'pincha yillar davomida sinov va xatolar orqali olingan saboqlardir.

Bundan tashqari, insondan o'rganish shaxsiy aloqani o'rnatadi va ko'pincha qimmatli aloqa imkoniyatlariga olib keladi. Aytishlaricha, "Tajriba eng yaxshi o'qituvchi", va tajribaga ega bo'lganlardan o'rganish undan keyingi eng yaxshi narsadir.

questions.prompt: Why do many people today prefer to learn new things using online tutorials?
questions.sampleA1: I like online. It is easy. I watch video. Learn new thing.
questions.sampleA2: I think many people like online tutorials because they are easy. You can watch them at home, and they are often free. I like to learn online because it is convenient and I can learn what I want.
questions.sampleB1: I think many people prefer online tutorials now because they are very convenient. For example, you can learn at any time and in any place. Also, online tutorials are often cheaper than going to a class. However, it can be difficult to stay motivated when you are learning alone.
questions.sampleB2: Well, the main draw is convenience, I'd say. With online tutorials, you can learn at your own pace, pausing and rewinding whenever you like, without having to commute anywhere. They're usually free or dirt cheap too, and there's a tutorial for pretty much anything at your fingertips. For busy people, that flexibility is hard to turn down.
questions.uzSampleA1: Menga onlayn yoqadi. Bu oson. Men video ko'raman. Yangi narsani o'rganaman.
questions.uzSampleA2: Menimcha, ko'p odamlarga onlayn darsliklar yoqadi, chunki ular oson. Ularni uyda tomosha qilish mumkin va ular ko'pincha bepul. Menga onlayn o'rganish yoqadi, chunki bu qulay va men xohlagan narsani o'rgana olaman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, ko'p odamlar hozir onlayn darsliklarni afzal ko'rishadi, chunki ular juda qulay.
Masalan, siz istalgan vaqtda va istalgan joyda o'rganishingiz mumkin. Shuningdek, onlayn darsliklar ko'pincha sinfga borishdan arzonroq.
Biroq, yolg'iz o'rganayotganda motivatsiyani saqlab qolish qiyin bo'lishi mumkin.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Nima uchun bugungi kunda ko'p odamlar yangi narsalarni onlayn darsliklar orqali o'rganishni afzal ko'rishlarining bir nechta sabablari bor.
Birinchidan, ular an'anaviy ta'lim muhitlari taklif qila olmaydigan moslashuvchanlik darajasini taqdim etadilar. Odamlar o'z tezliklarida o'rganishlari, o'qishlarini mavjud majburiyatlariga moslashtirishlari mumkin.
Ikkinchidan, narx muhim omil hisoblanadi; ko'plab onlayn manbalar bepul yoki rasmiy ta'limdan ancha arzon.
Va nihoyat, onlaynda mavjud bo'lgan mavzularning xilma-xilligi beqiyos bo'lib, deyarli har qanday qiziqish yoki ko'nikmani qondiradi.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Why do many people today prefer to learn new things using online tutorials?
idioms: the world is your oyster - "dunyo sizning qo'lingizda"
sentenceStarters: "In today's digital age, online tutorials have become..." - "Bugungi raqamli asrda onlayn darsliklar ... bo'ldi"
"Primarily, online learning offers..." - "Birinchi navbatda, onlayn ta'lim ... taklif qiladi"
"Moreover, people can learn at their own pace..." - "Bundan tashqari, odamlar o'z tezligida o'rganishi mumkin..."

questions.sampleAnswer:
In today's digital age, online tutorials have become incredibly popular, as we can see reflected in the second picture, and there are several reasons for this trend.
Primarily, online learning offers unmatched flexibility and convenience. People can learn anything at any time, from anywhere, without having to commute to a classroom or coordinate schedules with an instructor. This is especially appealing for those with busy lifestyles.
Additionally, online tutorials are often free or significantly cheaper than formal courses. Platforms like YouTube, Coursera, and Khan Academy provide access to world-class education at no cost.
Moreover, people can learn at their own pace – they can pause, rewind, and rewatch content as many times as needed. As they say, "Knowledge is power", and the internet has made that power accessible to everyone.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bugungi raqamli davrda onlayn darsliklar juda mashhur bo'lib ketdi, buni ikkinchi rasmda ham ko'rishimiz mumkin va bu tendentsiyaning bir nechta sabablari bor.

Avvalo, onlayn ta'lim misli ko'rilmagan moslashuvchanlik va qulaylikni taklif etadi. Odamlar istalgan vaqtda, istalgan joydan, sinfga borishga yoki o'qituvchi bilan jadvalni muvofiqlashtirishga hojat qolmasdan, istalgan narsani o'rganishlari mumkin. Bu, ayniqsa, band hayot tarziga ega bo'lganlar uchun juda jozibali.

Bundan tashqari, onlayn darsliklar ko'pincha bepul yoki rasmiy kurslarga qaraganda ancha arzon. YouTube, Coursera va Khan Academy kabi platformalar bepul holda jahon darajasidagi ta'limga kirish imkoniyatini beradi.

Bundan tashqari, odamlar o'z tezligida o'rganishlari mumkin – ular kerak bo'lganda kontentni to'xtatib turishlari, orqaga qaytarishlari va qayta-qayta ko'rishlari mumkin. Aytganlaridek, "Bilim – kuch", va internet bu kuchni hamma uchun ochiq qildi.

questions.prompt: Tell me about a time when you had to work under pressure.
questions.sampleA1: I... work... busy. Boss... angry. I... finish... work. Good!
questions.sampleA2: One time, I had a lot of work. It was very difficult and I was tired. I had to finish it quickly because my boss needed it. I finished it and my boss was happy.
questions.sampleB1: I remember a time when I had to work under a lot of pressure. It was when I was working on a project at university and the deadline was very soon. I had a lot of things to do and not much time. I think I managed it quite well by making a plan and focusing on the most important tasks. It was stressful, but I learned a lot.
questions.sampleB2: Right, let me tell you about a time I really had to work under pressure. It was during my final year at university, when I had three big exams crammed into a single week, and on top of that, a group project due on the Friday. To be honest, I bit off more than I could chew that semester, and for a while I felt completely snowed under. As for how I managed my time, the first thing I did was sit down and draw up a proper timetable. I broke everything into small, manageable chunks and tackled the hardest subjects first, while my brain was still fresh. I set aside a solid hour for each topic, then took a short break to recharge my batteries. I also had to cut out distractions completely — I logged out of social media and put my phone in another room. There were a couple of nights where I had to burn the midnight oil, but staying organised really paid off in the end. Do I think people work better under pressure? Honestly, I think it depends on the person. For some, a tight deadline gives them a real sense of urgency and sharpens their focus — they seem to rise to the occasion. For others, though, too much pressure just leads to stress and burnout, and their work suffers. Personally, I'd say a little pressure keeps me on my toes, but there's definitely a limit. As the saying goes, a bit of pressure can bring out the best in you — as long as it doesn't tip over into panic.

bulletPoints: Tell me about a time when you had to work under pressure.
How did you manage your time?
Do you think that people work better under pressure?
questions.sampleAnswer:
A time I worked under pressure:
One of the most stressful experiences I've had was during my final university exams last year. I had three major exams scheduled within the same week, and I desperately needed to pass all of them to graduate on time. The workload was absolutely overwhelming.
How I managed my time:
To cope with the pressure, I created a detailed study timetable, breaking each subject into manageable chunks. I strictly followed a schedule: studying for 50 minutes, then taking a 10-minute break. I also prioritised topics based on their difficulty and weight in the exam. Cutting out distractions like social media was essential.
Do people work better under pressure?
I think it really depends on the individual. Some people actually thrive under pressure – the tight deadline gives them a sense of urgency that boosts their focus. However, for others, excessive pressure leads to anxiety and burnout. Personally, I believe a moderate amount of pressure can be motivating, but too much is counterproductive. As they say, "Pressure makes diamonds", but only if applied the right way.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bosim ostida ishlagan vaqtim:
Mening eng stressli tajribalarimdan biri o'tgan yili universitetdagi yakuniy imtihonlar paytida bo'lgan. Bir hafta ichida uchta asosiy imtihonim bor edi va men ularning barchasidan o'z vaqtida bitirish uchun o'tishim kerak edi. Ish hajmi juda katta edi.
Vaqtimni qanday boshqarganim:
Bosimga bardosh berish uchun men har bir fanni boshqarish mumkin bo'lgan qismlarga bo'lib, batafsil o'quv jadvalini tuzdim. Men qat'iy jadvalga amal qildim: 50 daqiqa o'qish, keyin 10 daqiqalik tanaffus. Shuningdek, imtihondagi qiyinligi va og'irligiga qarab mavzularni ustuvor qilib belgiladim. Ijtimoiy tarmoqlar kabi chalg'ituvchi omillarni yo'q qilish juda muhim edi.
Odamlar bosim ostida yaxshiroq ishlaydimi?
Menimcha, bu shaxsga bog'liq. Ba'zi odamlar bosim ostida gullab-yashnaydi - qattiq muddat ularga diqqatini kuchaytiradigan shoshilinchlik hissini beradi. Biroq, boshqalar uchun haddan tashqari bosim xavotir va charchashga olib keladi. Shaxsan men, o'rtacha miqdordagi bosim rag'batlantirishi mumkin, ammo juda ko'pi samarasiz deb hisoblayman. Aytishlaricha, "Bosim olmos yaratadi", lekin faqat to'g'ri qo'llanilsa.

questions.prompt: Governments should stop funding space exploration and focus on solving problems on Earth.
questions.sampleA1: Space is... difficult. Money is for Earth. Earth is important.
questions.sampleA2: I think Earth is more important. Space is maybe good, but Earth has problems. People need food and houses. Space is for later, maybe.
questions.sampleB1: Well, I think Earth is more important right now. Space exploration is interesting, but it costs a lot of money. There are many problems on Earth, like poverty and sickness. So, I think governments should help people on Earth first. Maybe later they can spend money on space.
questions.sampleB2: Well, this is a real hot-button issue, and I can genuinely see the argument on both sides. On the one hand, those who want to cut off funding for space have a point. Space missions cost an absolute fortune, and that money could arguably be put towards more pressing issues here at home — things like poverty, healthcare and education. When millions of people are struggling to get by, it does seem hard to justify spending billions launching rockets into space. On top of that, our own planet is crying out for attention, with the climate crisis and pollution getting worse by the year and desperately in need of funding. On the other hand, though, I think scrapping space programmes altogether would be short-sighted. A huge amount of the technology we take for granted — GPS, weather forecasting, even certain medical devices — actually came out of space research. What's more, exploring space inspires young people to get into science and engineering, which pays off for society in the long run. And realistically, understanding the universe might be vital for our long-term survival as a species. So where do I stand? Personally, I don't think it has to be an either-or situation. Governments are perfectly capable of striking a balance — funding space exploration while still pouring resources into problems here on Earth, rather than treating it as a straight choice between the two. At the end of the day, cutting space funding entirely would mean throwing the baby out with the bathwater. I'd rather see us do both, just with sensible priorities.

for: Billions of dollars could be redirected to solve immediate issues like global poverty and healthcare.
Our own planet's environmental crises need urgent attention and funding before we look to other planets.

questions.sampleAnswer:
This is a highly debatable topic with compelling arguments on both sides.
Those who support ending space funding argue that the billions spent on space exploration could be better allocated to pressing issues right here on Earth. Indeed, with millions of people still living in poverty and lacking access to basic healthcare, it seems difficult to justify sending rockets into space. Furthermore, our planet is facing severe environmental crises – climate change, deforestation, and ocean pollution – that demand immediate attention and resources.
However, opponents make equally strong points. Space research has led to countless technological breakthroughs that we use daily, such as GPS, water filtration systems, and even memory foam. Additionally, space programmes inspire future generations to pursue careers in science and engineering, which ultimately benefits humanity. Understanding the universe is not a luxury – it's a necessity for our long-term survival.
Personally, I believe we shouldn't see this as an either/or situation. Governments can fund both space exploration and domestic programmes. As they say, "We cannot solve our problems with the same thinking we used when we created them". Space exploration pushes humanity to think differently.
